title: The Manifestation of Mercy in Day and Night
english: It signifies. I have said many times toward this point: that the punishment is diminished. Let it be said: let more people have done injustice; from these, some did not do injustice, but showed mercy. His punishment is diminished, and these things have not been done to him sluggishly. When someone previously sinned, he has the works 'going before him to judgment'. They run ahead of him, leading him on to the judgment. But other sins follow. When someone, while acting, does good and a few sins, these follow. 'Likewise', he says, 'also the good works'. As I have said concerning sins, so also concerning good works I will say. However, no one having done good remains without fault above. From it, his punishment is diminished. And he who 'did not know sin nor did it' (1 John 3:5) and the words of the lapses, has far from himself his salvation; he has his salvation pure, neither sin nor lapse being left to it, but not even this, the word of a lapse.

3 O my God, I have cried days to you, and you do not listen, and night, and it does not come to my mind (Ps 142:2). The state of the life of men is diverse. It has some profitable aspects, and it has some dark aspects. And in these human things there are days, which are called 'day', and dark things, which are named 'night'. This therefore he says: and in the pleasant and bright things toward you I cry, and you listen, and in the night I do this, and it does not come to my mind; for after your departure and the dark things no longer being unclear, it has become manifest to me. He listens to our crying in the days; and at night, that is to say, 27 being in the dark state, we have him helping, and in the matter we have received knowledge that he helps; for this is: 'and at night, and it does not come to my mind'. And even if it were to others that this were the case, if this were 'the man before God', he was abandoned, this was not to his mind; for he came to this voluntarily: 'I will go to myself toward the mountain of myrrh' (Song of Solomon 1:4). Myrrh...

His body has journeyed to the mountain, because on behalf of all those who were myrrh-soaked, he accepted death. As for why it is so, let us learn from another psalm: that the dark things are ignorance and night; 'by day,' he says, 'the Lord commands his mercy, and by night he will make it known' (Ps 92:2).

When we clearly and readily see men being pitied, God has commanded his mercy by day. And 'by night' he 'will make it known'; for if you know that God also punishes and hands over in order to make his mercy known—for he does not hand over men to punishments crudely—in this night, the dark one, he will establish it, and the mercy of God will be made known. And by day he commands the mercy when his mercy is manifest, and by night; it is possible [to manifest it] through the darkness of the state of those being punished. However, even if they also despair, he himself will make known even in the night his mercy.

'And not unto oblivion of me' (Ps 16:11); I do not cry out in ignorance at night, I do not cry out in ignorance that you listen. 'But you dwell among the saints, O praise of Israel' (Ps 67:35). See what he says: you who dwell among the saints and are the praise of all those having pure hearts and seeing you—for such people are Israel—you have not abandoned me; for if you dwell among the saints, and the saints suffer something, they were not abandoned; for how could you be in them, and not simply, but the praise of Israel?

And it is also possible that 'but you dwell among the saints' means this: even if you have surrounded some with a pitiful death and it seems to [one] that you have withdrawn from me, yet in the saints, in those I teach, in those I think upon, you dwell. If you are in these, I have not been abandoned. And it is possible for the holy things to be taken also upon the blessed logical beings, and upon the holy men, and upon the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens. For God, being present everywhere, is found in such things, and all such things are his temple, a multi-purpose temple. Therefore, [you] are a praise in Israel; for he truly...
